taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (by core mechanic), using only the provided rules

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; bulbs can’t illuminate each other; each white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color black cells so each number equals the count of white cells from the number to the nearest black cell or frame (horizontally+vertically); numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.

### B) Black/white (or shaded/unshaded) region formation
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells must form rectangles/squares; orthogonally connected white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give size of the area containing the cell.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold borders) with numbers = count of painted cells; white cells can’t stretch across >2 rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
- **Hitori**: No duplicate numbers in any row/column among white cells; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-bordered territories have numbers indicating how many more of one mark they get (with special cases); “—” limited vertically/horizontally extension; “|” limited similarly.
- **Kurotto**: Color cells black; circle number = sum of continuous black cells extending from it (orthogonally); empty circles may have any number; circle cells can’t be colored.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, color four consecutive squares (tetromino); similarly shaped tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares form a connected network; no 2×2 or larger all-colored squares.
- **Nurikabe**: Numbers indicate size of continuous white regions; each white region has exactly one number; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2 or larger.
- **Nurimeizu**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 group entirely shaded.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade some cells; each outlined region contains exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 group entirely shaded.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares (four kinds); cannot place in black squares; uncovered white cells must form a rectangle or square; numbers indicate how many black triangles are around it orthogonally.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold borders) have a number = count of continuous black cells in that room; rooms with no number any; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; after “dropping” stones straight down, stones must fill bottom half with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered tiles are colored; diagonal-line cell number gives count of black cells to the right or downward along that line/column until grid edge or another diagonal-number cell; all cells of a tile are either all colored or all uncolored; final picture outlines an object.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; cells with numbers cannot be colored; each rectangle bordered by bold lines has exactly one wrong number (wrong colored-cell count); colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.
- **Yajilin**: Draw a single loop; loop passes through centers; loop must not pass through black cells or numbered cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.

### C) Loop / path drawing (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no crossing/branching/revisiting; must pass all white-circle cells; in each bold-enclosed area, loop either goes straight through all white circles or turns right-angled at all of them; must not go through black-circle cells.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; passes all circles; white circles require straight-through and a right-angled turn in at least one adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn at the circle cell then straight through next cell on both sides.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; passes through arrow cells; loop direction follows arrows; wind direction blocks movement against wind; when entering a wind-blown cell from the side, must move at least one cell in that direction; cannot hit borders or enter black cells when bent by side wind.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no crossing/branching/revisiting; must pass all black circles with each black circle as midpoint of the straight segment passing through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; passes through each room only once; once it leaves a room it can’t return; in each room it goes through all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); after moons in one room, next room entered must be suns, and vice versa.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms (bold borders) each contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicated in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ the value.
- **Slitherlink**: Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop; numbers indicate how many lines surround the cell; empty cells any; loop never crosses or branches.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; dotted segments between black cells or outer frame are “Gates”; loop must pass all Gates but each Gate only once; loop starts/returns to open numbered circle; open circle number = number of Gates to go through; black cells at Gate ends show when loop crosses; Gate without number can be crossed anywhere.
- **Yajilin**: (also in B) single loop through centers; must not pass through black cells or numbered cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.

### D) Number placement / arithmetic in cells (non-loop)
- **Chained Block**: Fill blocks of consecutive black cells; number indicates size of the block containing the cell (or “?” unknown); every block must contain one number or “?”; blocks in corner contact form chains; all blocks part of a chain; chain can’t contain more than one block of the same size/shape (rotation/mirror considered same).
- **Evolomino**: Draw squares in some white cells; orthogonally connected group = block; each block has exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow; each arrow path passes through at least two blocks; subsequent blocks on an arrow route add one square without rotating/flipping.
- **Fillomino**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; board divided into blocks; each block filled with same number horizontally or vertically; block size equals the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges equal to the island number; max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/other bridges; bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Hebi**: Place numbers in snake parts so 1→5 are sequentially connected in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snake parts can’t be in squares adjacent to next black square or rim; black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with digits from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; each cell has only one digit.
- **Norinori**: Place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils; draw lines from pencil tip through cells; pencil is straight group with tip at one end; line passes through centers orthogonally/turning; numbered cell gives pencil length; line from tip goes through as many cells as the number; pencil line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Ripple Effect**: (also in C) rooms contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; duplication distance constraint.
- **Satogaeri**: “Countries” are bold-bordered; move circles so each country has exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells they must pass through; circles without numbers may move any distance but some don’t; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Sudoku**: Place 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all numbers 1–9.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles with numbers in cells; each rectangle contains only one number showing the number of cells in the rectangle.
- **Shakashaka**: (also in B) numbers indicate count of black triangles around it orthogonally.
- **Tilepaint**: (also in B) diagonal-line cell numbers determine counts of black cells to right/down along that line/column.
- **Yosenabe**: Move circles orthogonally into gray areas; arrow shows movement with tip in a gray cell; arrows don’t bend and don’t cross other circles or other arrows; number in gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas any sum but at least one circle must enter a gray area.
- **Yajilin**: (also in C/B) numbers show how many black cells in arrow direction; loop constraints exclude numbered cells.

### E) Tiling / block partitioning constraints
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines over dotted lines; each block contains a pair of areas of white and gray cells with same form (rotation/mirror allowed); number indicates number of cells of that color in the block (half the block’s total cells of that color); block can contain any number of cells with the number.
- **Five Cells**: Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; no blocks with 0–4 or 6+ cells; number in a cell shows how many lines of a block are around it (including outer frame); as many as 5 numbered cells in a block; lines must surround a cell and cannot enter a block.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (also in D) bridges connect islands; not a partition, but still uses “blocks” concept? (No—so keep only in D.)
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: (also in B) outlined regions and blocks inside them.
- **Sashigane**: Divide grid into L-shaped blocks one block wide; all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles form the knee (bend); open circle number gives number of cells in its block; arrows form one end pointing toward the knee; number of marks in a block (arrows or open circles) may be 0–3.
- **Sashigane**: (also in D) uses counts on marks.
- **Evolomino**: (also in D) blocks connected to arrows; route adds one square.
- **Chained Block**: (also in D) blocks are consecutive black cells; chain constraints.
- **Shikaku**: (also in D) rectangles partition grid.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms partition grid by bold lines.

### F) Connectivity constraints (graph-like)
- **Akari**: illumination connectivity along rows/columns (visibility constraint).
- **Hashiwokakero**: bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Hitori**: white cells form a continuous network.
- **Kurodoko**: all white cells must be connected.
- **Nagareru**: loop is single continuous loop.
- **Nurikabe**: black cells linked as continuous wall.
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: all shaded cells connected across regional boundaries.
- **Numberlink**: connect pairs of same numbers with continuous line; lines can’t cross/branch/reuse cells; lines can’t go through number cells.
- **Satogaeri**: circles can’t cross tracks; movement constraints.
- **Yosenabe**: circles move into gray areas; arrows don’t cross.

### G) Line/edge constraints without a loop (or with special line behavior)
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs with continuous lines; lines go through centers; orthogonal/turning; never twice through same cell; lines can’t cross/branch off/go through number cells.
- **Pencils**: pencil lines from tips; straight group; can turn; can’t cross/branch.
- **Nagareru**: loop with wind-direction restrictions (special movement rules).
- **Yajilin**: loop with exclusion of black/numbered cells and black adjacency restriction.

### H) Pure numeric/sequence constraints (no explicit loop)
- **Nansuke**: digits placed in up-down or left-right orientation; each cell has one digit.
- **Ripple Effect**: consecutive numbers per room; duplication distance rule.
- **Sudoku**: standard row/column/block completeness.
- **Hebi**: sequential 1→5 snake connectivity with directional attack constraints.
- **Chained Block**: block sizes and chain uniqueness.

If you want, I can also produce a second taxonomy that groups games by **output type** (place bulbs / shade cells / draw bridges / draw loop / draw paths / partition into rectangles/blocks / place digits) while still using only these rules.
